title: Research note: bounded 112-port transvection boundary census
body:
## Result

Adds a bounded negative result for the selected pair-0 stage-0 forward / stage-1 backward boundary. Across all 112 pinned port pairs, the verifier checks every directed coordinate transvection `T_ij = I + E_ij` on `F_2^9`:

- Each port has compatible maps: 77 ports have 6 and 35 ports have 42, for 1,932 incidences.
- No one coordinate transvection works at every port.
- `RESULT.json` records the exact per-port candidate sets.

The profile-only cost screen grants the mechanism two deleted rank-one boundary transitions per port and charges one rank-one shear. The selected local rank-one count falls from 2,412 to 21,701/9 per call. Its exact `a`-ceiling rises from `1690054109089/10^15` to `338060003381/200000000000000` (0.01455%), weakening this bound. No new construction, legal composition, supplier integration, or `kappa` is claimed.

## Reproduction

```sh
python3 -I -B research/rank1-transvection-boundary-seed0410/verify.py
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/rank1-transvection-boundary-seed0410 --check-only
```

Both the exact verifier and metadata/pin check passed locally on Python 3.14. The repository package runner requires Python 3.12, which is unavailable in this environment; no local registered replay or hosted-CI result is claimed. The PR workflow can run the declared Python 3.12 replay.
